turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files:
  - b3_te_zt900_train.csv: 300 real samples, columns process/composition
    columns (O, Sb, Co, Si, Sn, Ca, Ni, Ti, Pb, Se, Ge, Cu, Zr, Te, S, Zn,
    Fe, Yb, Mn, Sr, Nb, Bi, Cd, Hf, In) and `target` (the measured zT
    (thermoelectric figure of merit) at 900 K).
  - b3_te_zt900_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE samples whose zT (thermoelectric
    figure of merit) at 900 K was NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and
    the same process/composition columns.

Using the training data, predict which candidates have the HIGHEST zT
(thermoelectric figure of merit) at 900 K, then select the 5 best candidates
from the pool.

Reason from the training data, then end your answer with an explicit ranked
list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904,
c905".
turns.answer_text:
The highest measured zT values in the training set (>2) belong exclusively to Pb-chalcogenide compositions that mix Te with S (or Se) near the 50 at.% Pb line. The single pool member that falls in this family is c052 (Pb \(\approx\) 0.493, Te \(\approx\) 0.394, S \(\approx\) 0.099), which is compositionally adjacent to the training point that recorded zT = 2.21 and is therefore ranked first.

The next-highest training cluster (zT 1.16–1.74) consists of near-stoichiometric Cu\(_2\)Se. Two pool entries match this chemistry: c054 (slightly Cu-deficient, nearest the 1.74 point) and c063 (nearest the 1.45 point). They occupy ranks 2 and 4.

A tightly grouped set of PbSe samples yields zT 1.19–1.40; the pool analogue c012 (Pb \(\approx\) 0.50, Se \(\approx\) 0.498) is therefore placed third.

The strongest remaining family is the half-Heusler n-type SnNi(Zr,Hf) alloys (training zT up to 1.35). Candidate c078 is essentially identical to the two highest members of that family and is ranked fifth.

All other pool chemistries (oxides, Si-Ge, filled skutterudites, BiCuSeO, SnTe, \ldots) correspond to training zT values well below 1.1 and are discarded.

Final: c052, c054, c012, c063, c078
